title: feat(core): persistence units declared by a runtime's unit source (Vidocq/vidocq#551)
body:
Noether side of Vidocq/vidocq#551 (persistence units from `vidocq.persistence."<unit>".*` keys). Noether reads no
Vidocq key: it gains a container-neutral SPI, and the Vidocq Noether extension implements it in a follow-up PR on
the vidocq repository.

## Why

A unit is declared in a `persistence.xml` only, or in code with `PersistenceConfiguration`, which `noether-jpa-cdi`
never sees. A runtime that configures everything else with its own keys (Vidocq, Quarkus) needs to declare units the
same way, and to point a `persistence.xml` unit at a production pool or change a property per deployment.

## What

- **SPI** `io.vidocq.noether.jpa.core.spi.PersistenceUnitSource` (`List<PersistenceUnitDeclaration> units(ClassLoader)`),
  found with `ServiceLoader` in Noether's module layer, then through the application's loader (`uses` in
  `module-info.java`). `PersistenceUnits` merges what the sources return with the files, so the provider and
  `PersistenceDescriptors` (hence `noether-jpa-cdi`) see the same units.
- **`PersistenceUnitDeclaration`**, an immutable value with a builder. Its attributes fall in two groups (the
  maintainer's decision 1 on vidocq#551):
  - *declaring*: root, packages, listed classes, transaction type, qualifiers, scope. A unit of the same name in a
    `persistence.xml` or another source is the noether#78 duplicate. The message now names the file and the source:
    "a unit source may only override the data sources and the properties of a unit that a persistence.xml declares";
  - *overriding*: JTA / non-JTA data sources and properties. With only these, the declaration overrides the file's
    unit (its properties win), or declares the unit at its `defaultRoot` when no file declares it.
- **`defaultRoot` / `defaultTransactionType`**: what a declaration that only overrides uses when it ends up declaring
  the unit (no file declares it). They declare nothing, so a runtime whose units are JTA by default can still only
  override a `persistence.xml` unit.
- **Where the sources are found**: Noether's module layer, Noether's own class loader, then the application's.
  `vidocq:generate` runs Noether on its processor path with a loader that lists the application's resources only,
  so a runtime's source next to Noether is found there.
- **`whenAlone()`**: a runtime's default unit (decision 2). It is declared only when the application declares no other
  unit and its root holds a managed class (the class files are scanned, as for any unit).
- **Packages**: `PersistenceUnitDefinition.managedPackages`, so a unit keeps the classes of its root to some packages
  and their sub-packages (`ManagedClasses`).
- Docs: `usage.adoc`, new section "Units declared by a runtime"; the CDI section names the unit sources.

Decision 3 (a build-time key changed at start fails the start) is the Vidocq extension's job: Noether asks the
sources at build and at start alike.

## Tests

- `UnitSourcesTest` (10): declare, list the classes, override a file unit, override without a file, duplicate with a
  file, duplicate between sources, the default transaction type, and the default unit (declared alone, not beside another unit, not with an empty
  root). Red first: with the merge disabled, 7 of 9 fail (the 2 negative cases pass by construction).
- `ManagedClassesTest` (+2): the package restriction keeps sub-packages and matches whole package names.
- `noether-jpa-processor-module-it`: a module that `provides PersistenceUnitSource`, and
  `Persistence.createEntityManagerFactory("processor-from-source")` on the module path. Red without the `provides`:
  "No Persistence provider for EntityManager named processor-from-source".
- Full reactor `./mvnw verify`: green (core 960).

title: test(architecture): no private lookup or member found by name outside the documented adapters
body:
Stacked on #81 (architecture rules): review and merge after it; only the last commit is new.

## Why

The shared `noReflection` rule of `vidocq-archrules` flags `java.lang.reflect` and the reflective calls of `Class`,
but not the `java.lang.invoke` route to the same members: `MethodHandles.privateLookupIn`, `Lookup.find*`,
`Lookup.unreflect*`. So `access.Handles`, which creates converters and reads `@EnumeratedValue` fields through a
private lookup, was not listed anywhere. The ecosystem-wide fix is Vidocq/vidocq-parent#34; this PR holds Noether to
it now with a local rule, removed once the shared rule covers the route.

## What

- `ArchitectureRules.NO_DEEP_LOOKUP`: no call to `MethodHandles.privateLookupIn` or to `MethodHandles.Lookup.find*` /
  `unreflect*` outside the reflective fallbacks and `DEEP_LOOKUP_ADAPTERS`. Defining a hidden class and combining or
  invoking handles stay free.
- `DEEP_LOOKUP_ADAPTERS`: one entry, `access.Handles`, with its reason. The other deep lookups of the shipped classes
  (`AccessGenerator`, `RuntimeMetamodel`, `ResultConstructors`, `ConnectionSources`) are already reflective fallbacks.
- Self-tests: three fixtures the rule catches (`privateLookupIn` + `findGetter`, `publicLookup().findVirtual`,
  `unreflectConstructor`), two look-alikes it keeps (`defineHiddenClass`, `MethodHandles.dropArguments`), and the
  stale-entry guard (each adapter must still be reported by the rule with no adapter).
- Docs: `internals.adoc` (Reflective fallbacks), `reference.adoc`, `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`.

## Tests

`./mvnw -pl noether-architecture-tests -am test -Dtest='ArchitectureRules*'`: 51 tests, green. Red first with a stub
rule: the three breach fixtures were not caught.

title: fix(core): a record id class is built in the order of its components
body:
## Why

Found while generating the id class accesses (#83): the bootstrap built a record `@IdClass` by passing the identifier attributes to its canonical constructor in the order the entity declares them (BUG-20261114-05).

- Components of the same types in another order: the values were swapped. With `@Id String aisle; @Id String place;` and `record BoothKey(String place, String aisle)`, `PersistenceUnitUtil.getIdentifier` returned `BoothKey[place=A, aisle=7]` for aisle `A`, place `7`.
- Components of other types in another order: the constructor was not found and the unit failed to start.

## What

- `MappedUnit.idClassAccess` reads the component order of a record id class from its class file (its instance fields, through `ClassFileSource`: no reflection added).
- `Accesses.ofRecord` builds the record's access in component order and, when that order differs, wraps it in the new `ReorderedAccess`, which lists the attributes in the entity's order and permutes `construct` and `get`.
- `BUG.md`: BUG-20261114-05, fixed.

## Tests

`RecordIdClassTest` (red before): the identifier of an entity is the record of its own values; an entity is found by its record key, once per persistence context; a record of components of other types in another order builds the identifier. Core (951), module-its, JTA and CDI suites green locally.

Independent of #81–#84; #83 touches the same method (`idClassAccess`), so whichever merges second is rebased.

title: fix(processor): a result class of a closed package needs no exports
body:
**Stacked on #83 (itself on #82)**: review the last commit only; this branch is rebased onto `main` as they merge.

## Why

Generate at compile time whatever can be, reflection at start time being only the fallback for what `noether-jpa-processor` did not process. A constructor expression (§4.8.2) or a `@ConstructorResult` (§3.11.15) unreflected the public constructors of its class from the core, which needs the class's package exported to Noether: on the module path, a named query building a result class of a closed package failed (BUG-20261114-04).

## What

- New SPI class `ResultConstructorAccess` (the public constructors of a class, in declaration order, and `construct(index, arguments)`), and a default method `ManagedAccessProvider.resultConstructors()`.
- `noether-jpa-processor` writes `<Class>$$NoetherConstructors` for each class a `@NamedQuery` constructor expression (also repeated, or in `@NamedQueries`) or a `@SqlResultSetMapping` constructor result names, calling the constructors with `new` from the class's package. The package provider hands them over.
- `MappedUnit` indexes them by class and name; `ResultConstructors` takes them before the reflective lookup; the `Translator` resolves the class of a constructor expression through them before `Class.forName`; JPQL and native queries read the constructors once per query.
- Left reflective, as before: a class only a query built at run time names (`createQuery`, Criteria `construct`: APT cannot see these strings), an abstract or inner class, a class with a public constructor that declares a checked exception.
- Docs: usage (queries, module path), getting-started and internals (generated classes). `BUG.md`: BUG-20261114-04 fixed for the classes the sources name.

## Tests

- Processor `ResultConstructorsTest` (4, red before): which classes get constructors, declaration order and primitive parameters, a record of a result-set mapping, incremental build.
- Core `ResultConstructorsTest`: the generated candidates, and the wrapping of a constructor's exception, as on the reflective path.
- `ClosedPackageCodeModulePathTest`: a named query (red before, `IllegalAccessException`) and a result-set mapping building a record of a package neither exported nor opened.
- Processor, core (950), module-its, JTA and CDI suites green locally.

title: fix(processor): an @IdClass of a closed package needs no opens
body:
**Stacked on #82**: its commit (converters and `@EnumeratedValue` enums) is the first one of this branch. Review the second commit only; this branch is rebased onto `main` once #82 is merged.

## Why

The user's direction: generate at compile time whatever can be, reflection at start time being only the fallback for archives `noether-jpa-processor` did not process. An `@IdClass` was still always served by the start-time hidden class (`Accesses.of`), which needs the package of the id class opened to Noether: on the module path, an entity keyed by an id class of a closed package failed to start (BUG-20261114-03).

## What

- `noether-jpa-processor` writes `<IdClass>$$NoetherIdAccess` for the id class of an entity it serves (same module, compiled from source), listing the attributes the bootstrap lists: one per identifier attribute, in their order, by field when the id class or a superclass declares a non-static field of that name, else by property. The part for a relationship of a derived identity has the type the id class declares (§2.4.1.1). The nearest `@IdClass` of the hierarchy applies, as at bootstrap. The rule sits in `IdClassMembers`.
- `MappedUnit.idClassAccess` takes the generated access matching those attributes before `Accesses.of`.
- Left to the bootstrap, as before: a relationship part without a field of its name (§2.4.1.3 example 5a), a field whose type is not the identifier attribute's, a record whose components do not follow the identifier attributes.
- Incremental builds keep the id accesses of the package while the id class exists.
- Docs: getting-started (generated classes), usage (module path), internals (generated code). `BUG.md`: BUG-20261114-03 fixed.

## Tests

- `IdClassesTest` (7, red before the change): field, property, record, record in another order, derived identity with and without a field, incremental build.
- `ClosedPackageCodeModulePathTest.anIdClassOfTheClosedPackageFindsTheEntity`: the module path, the package neither exported nor opened; red before (`IllegalAccessException`), green after.
- Processor, core (948), module-its, JTA and CDI suites green locally.

title: fix(processor): converters and @EnumeratedValue enums of a closed package need no opens
body:
## Converters and `@EnumeratedValue` enums of a closed package need no `opens`

Fixes BUG-20261114-01 and BUG-20261114-02, the first two of four bugs that the compile-time review of Noether's reflective sites turned up.

### The bugs

An application module compiled with `noether-jpa-processor` declared `provides … with <pkg>._NoetherJpaAccess`, and its package was neither exported nor opened. That application failed to start as soon as an attribute went through either of these, from that package:

- a converter: `Noether cannot access the class ….Shout`;
- an enum mapped by its `@EnumeratedValue` field: `… ….Tier`.

The core reached both through a private lookup, and a private lookup needs the package opened. The error message also asked for the processor and the `provides` clause, which the application already had.

### The fix

- **Converter**: the processor generates `<Converter>$$NoetherAccess`, an access with no attribute. Its `instantiate()` calls the no-arg constructor from the converter's package, through a handle when that constructor is private.
- **`@EnumeratedValue` enum**: the processor generates `<Enum>$$NoetherAccess`, a new read-only shape of `AccessWriter`. Its one attribute is the `@EnumeratedValue` field: no instantiation, no setter.
- **`ValueBinders` takes them first**, through `MappedUnit`'s index of generated accesses. The private lookup stays the fallback for classes compiled without the processor.
- **Packages and modules**:
  - a package that holds only a converter or such an enum gets its provider too;
  - a module that does not read `io.vidocq.noether.jpa.core`, such as a library of converters, is left to the bootstrap without error;
  - incremental builds keep these accesses (`stillManaged`).

### Tests (red first)

- `noether-jpa-processor-module-it`, `ClosedPackageCodeModulePathTest`: a converter and an `@EnumeratedValue` enum of the closed package. Both were red before the fix, with the error above.
- `noether-jpa-processor`, `ConvertersAndEnumsTest`:
  - a package with no entity gets its provider;
  - a converter with a private constructor;
  - the enum access is read-only;
  - an incremental build keeps the accesses.
- Local run passes, with `noether-jpa-core`, `-processor`, `-processor-module-it`, `-module-it`, `-cdi` and `-cdi-module-it` built together (`-am verify`).

### Still open

The two other bugs come next, in their own pull requests:

- BUG-20261114-03: an `@IdClass` of a closed package; the processor never serves id classes;
- BUG-20261114-04: a `SELECT NEW` result class of a closed package.

Docs: Getting started (generated classes), Usage (module path) and Internals (Generated code).
